correctness.rationale: For every d>=3,n>=2d+5, directed-cycle synchronous dynamics shifts the four-bit support one step per time. Pairwise edge-step distinctions imply each outer edge {i,i+d+1} is confined to a unique maximal facet; the two specified stages give n tetrahedron/free-triangle and n triangle/free-edge elementary collapses. The final two triangle orbits are an embedded quotient of the standard triangular square grid by the rank-two lattice a+db=0 mod n. Therefore the quotient is a torus. Actual standalone checks exactly rerun all elementary free-coface conditions and orientable six-cycle vertex links for 190 pairs; finite checks support but are not substituted for the proof. Cup nontriviality follows from torus cohomology.

value.rationale: Riihimäki–Smith (2026), Section 5 explicitly asks whether any avalanche complexes fail to be wedges of spheres. This infinite two-parameter directed-cycle family answers that structural existence question within the original model, and its nonvanishing degree-one cup product is a decisive stronger invariant than Betti numbers. The 2n elementary collapse also supplies uniform, reproducible geometry instead of a small-case census.
